justification: Changes a displayed lot measurement and one input to the granny-flat eligibility request, but touches no database, no stored data and no auth. Above minor because a wrong number reaches users and a rule input; below critical because the new value is never larger than the true frontage and null is handled by every consumer.

falsifiable_check.observed_red: 5 failed / 5 when the new test file was run against origin/main's lot-dimensions.ts (MUTATION, measured 2026-10-18); with the change all 5 pass.
falsifiable_check.fails_when: The one-segment-per-side logic returns. MUTATION: the 5 new tests were run against origin/main's lot-dimensions.ts: 5 failed / 5. With the change: geometry suites 4/4, 96 tests pass. Full jest 141 suites / 1978 tests pass. tsc --noEmit 0 errors.
falsifiable_check.external_authority: The real boundary ring of 6 Berrigan Street, Winston Hills (Lot 23 DP217713, 688 m2), returned by the live /api/property on 2026-10-18, and the Python implementation in services/lot_dimensions.py (PR #499), which gives frontage 22.4 and depth 39.7 on the same ring.

pre_impl.existing_data: Boundary segments from /api/property (12 segments for Lot 23 DP217713). One side of that lot is a curve stored as eight 1.67 m pieces. No table or column is written.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The old calculateLotDimensions took one segment per side with boundaries.find(), assuming one segment per side. A curved side is many segments, so depth came out as (1.67 + 6.14)/2 = 3.9 m and Site Controls showed frontage 38.4 m x depth 3.9 m for a 688 m2 lot. The new code works from the whole ring and does not rely on segment count.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Applies to every lot at render time. Nothing is stored, so existing lots get the new numbers on next view.
pre_impl.external_source_error: Not applicable: no external call was added. If the ring is missing or has fewer than three distinct points, the function returns null for frontage and depth.
pre_impl.frontend_type: Yes. frontage and depth in types/property.ts are now number | null. Consumers checked: effective-lot-width.ts (positiveFiniteOrNull), LepControls (?? null), StateLevelControls (|| null), see/propertyContext (sanitizeNumber), assessment/full route (lotWidth optional). All already handle null.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Where the polygon fills under 60% of its minimum bounding rectangle (L-shapes, strong curves), the display reads Not measured instead of a number. The granny-flat route omits frontage_m when the value is null or not above zero.

functions.name: frontageDepthFromRect
functions.input: closed boundary ring (array of points) from the property boundary data
functions.output: { frontage, depth } in metres: shorter side of the minimum-area rectangle is frontage, longer side is depth
functions.if_none: returns null for both when the ring has too few points or the polygon fills less than MIN_RECT_FILL (0.6) of the rectangle

functions.name: minAreaRect
functions.input: convex hull points computed from the boundary ring
functions.output: smallest-area rotated rectangle found by rotating calipers
functions.if_none: returns null for an empty or degenerate hull

functions.name: convexHull
functions.input: array of x/y points from the boundary ring
functions.output: array of hull points in order
functions.if_none: returns the input unchanged when under three points

functions.name: calculateLotDimensions
functions.input: boundary data from the property object
functions.output: frontage and depth (number | null) to the Site Controls display and the CDC calculator
functions.if_none: frontage and depth are null; display shows Not measured

values.if_missing: Shows Not measured with a note that the street-facing side is not identified

values.guard_at: same file, sent only when non-null and above zero for rectangular lots
values.if_missing: Field is left out of the request; the downstream eligibility step runs without a frontage input

break_it.scenario: A rotated lot, or a ring that starts at an arbitrary vertex, gives a different answer depending on the start point.
break_it.what_happens: Frontage and depth would change between page loads for the same lot.
break_it.how: lot-dimensions-rect.test.ts: rotated 15x40 rectangle returns the same result from every start vertex.

break_it.scenario: A side is split into many small segments (the Winston Hills curve).
break_it.what_happens: Old code returned depth 3.9 m for a lot that is 39.7 m long.
break_it.how: Test cuts one side into 10 pieces and checks the result equals the unsplit rectangle; the real Winston Hills ring returns 22.4 / 39.7.

break_it.scenario: An L-shaped or heavily curved lot is forced into a rectangle.
break_it.what_happens: A confident but meaningless width and length would be shown.
break_it.how: lot-dimensions.ts returns null when the polygon fills under 60% of the rectangle; the UI shows Not measured. Test: L-shape returns null.

break_it.scenario: A wide lot, where the street side is the longer side.
break_it.what_happens: The shorter side is labelled Width, which is not the street frontage.
break_it.how: Labels changed to Width / Length with a note that the street-facing side is not identified. For the granny-flat minimum-frontage test the shorter side is never more than the true frontage, so the test cannot pass wrongly on it. Test: wide 30x15 lot gives width 15.

mutation_analysis: The 5 new tests were run against origin/main's lot-dimensions.ts: 5 failed / 5, so each test depends on the new logic. With the change: geometry suites 4/4 (96 tests) pass; full jest 141 suites / 1978 tests pass; tsc --noEmit reports 0 errors.
residual_risk: The street-facing side is still not identified (a planned upgrade named in the PR #499 docstring), so Width is the shorter side and not always the frontage. Battleaxe lot display is unchanged. Lots that fail the 60% fill test show Not measured rather than a number.

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes, one check: open 6 Berrigan Street, Winston Hills after deploy and read Site Controls; expect width 22.4 m and length 39.7 m.
